name: navbar
title: Navbar
purpose: Provide responsive application navigation with compact item-anchored desktop menus plus controllable material, layout, and scroll behavior without coupling to a router or store.
accessibility: Uses labelled navigation landmarks and native links.
Expandable controls expose aria-expanded, aria-controls, and accessible names.
Escape closes an open desktop dropdown and all destinations remain available without hover.
The navigate event exposes the original uncancelled MouseEvent so router integration can preserve modifier clicks and native fallback.
commonMistakes: Coupling Navbar to a specific router.
Using the compact dropdown for a large unstructured navigation inventory.
Using fixed or reveal behavior without reserving space or scroll margin for page content.
Overriding Glassmorphism's floating glass treatment without a deliberate reason.

examples.title: Floating glass
examples.description: An inset translucent slab keeps surrounding background detail visible.
examples.source:
<script setup lang="ts">
import Navbar from "@/components/ui/Navbar.vue";
import Link from "@/components/ui/Link.vue";

// Placeholder navigation data for this documentation example.
const logo = { title: "BALSA UI", alt: "Balsa UI placeholder", href: "#top" };
const items = [
  {
    title: "Product",
    link: "#product",
    links: [
      { title: "Overview", link: "#overview", shortDescription: "A concise product introduction." },
      { title: "Release notes", link: "#releases", shortDescription: "What changed in the latest version." },
    ],
  },
  { title: "Solutions", link: "#solutions" },
  { title: "Resources", link: "#resources" },
];
</script>

<template>
  <Navbar :logo="logo" :items="items" type="floating" variant="glass" behavior="fixed">
  <template #actions>
    <Link href="#sign-in" size="sm">Sign in</Link>
    <Link href="#get-started" variant="solid" size="sm">Get started</Link>
  </template>
</Navbar>
</template>

props.name: contentRegion
props.description:
Optional CSS width for the desktop navigation region while the bar itself
stays full width, for a route whose page reserves the remainder. The
content centres inside the region and takes a taller row, reading as chrome
over a full-bleed page; below `lg` it always spans the bar.
